method: N+1 temperature nodes at x=i*L/N. Control widths are dx inside and dx/2 at either boundary; their sum is L, with no added mass or heat capacity. For each node C_i*dT_i/dt = net heat flux into its control volume. Backward Euler couples convection and radiation evaluated at the actual boundary temperature unknown; Newton uses the exact derivative of the fourth-power surface law. The inherited Thomas solver is only a linear-algebra backend.
flux_interpretation: The end-segment conductive gradient gives flux at the first INTERIOR control-volume face, not necessarily the exterior surface flux. At the upper half-volume: q_environment - k*(T_last-T_previous)/dx = rho*cp*(dx/2)*dT_last/dt. Their difference is explicitly stored heat, not an unbalanced massless boundary. A piecewise-linear nodal temperature interpolant is not claimed to satisfy the exterior derivative condition pointwise.
energy: H=rho*cp*sum_i(width_i*(T_i-20)), J/m2. Sum of nodal widths is exactly the original thickness. H equals the integral of the piecewise-linear temperature profile. Also retain exact profile integrals of eta*T and T^2 for future mechanics; do not project them onto fixed fibers in this iteration. Distinguish H-H_initial from H for initially hot verification cases.
startup: Initial temperatures are 20 C everywhere, including the surfaces, with zero sensible heat for the step case. At t=0 a nonzero environmental flux produces the semi-discrete initial temperature rate of the boundary half-volume; no temperature or energy jump is imposed. Positive-time profiles are solved steps, not a rescaled V11M field. Time interpolation between saved steps would still require a separate accuracy qualification.
source_policy: Properties, geometry, exposure coefficients and analytical-method references are inherited from V11K; none is newly calibrated to WTC. V11M/O/F remain saved controls and are not rerun. New nodal calculations are justified by the changed thermal discretization and V11O startup failure.
